title: Road — Classic

rows.text: Road — Classic
72 draft packages. Images have no embedded text; wording listed as an overlay is rendered separately.
ENC-C01-A · Smaller government
DOGE fired the park’s cleaners. The remaining ranger hasn’t had lunch. She offers your crew gloves beside overflowing bins. “Congratulations. You’re the smaller government.”
Share some food and help clear the bins → You share lunch and haul bags until your back aches. She hands you a bin liner. “Uniform allowance.”
Photograph the mess for your D.C. case → You photograph the overflowing bins. She points at the flies. “Only department still recruiting.”
Scene: A tired ranger offers unused gloves toward the watching travelers; nobody has accepted them. Overflowing bins crowd out the picnic furniture; flies hover over the only busy department.
Source: The administration fired about 1000 newly hired NPS staff in February 2025, including maintenance and cleaning roles. Do not pr…
ENC-C01-B · Permission to spin

At a roadside repair co-op, a mechanic shows you Oregon’s law limiting software locks on spare parts. Volunteers need some food and help salvaging switches. A washing machine rejects a working replacement. It accepts dirty underwear without checking the manufacturer.
Share some food; salvage switches → You share lunch and wrench out switches until your wrists ache. The drum can spin. The company’s permission is still buffering.
Photograph the lockout and Oregon law → You save the error and Oregon’s rule for D.C. The replacement fits perfectly. Ownership seems to be the incompatible part.

Scene: The mechanic holds a replacement switch beside an unlettered machine display while a volunteer indicates the unopened salvage bin; travelers consider helping. A machine full of mismatched socks accepts the laundry while its screen rejects the neatly fitting replacement control.
Editable overlays: “PART NOT RECOGNIZED” — Blank washing-machine display
Source: Oregon Revised Statutes: Right to Repair Consumer Equipment (2025 codification)
ENC-C01-C · Dignity, by the pound

Rubio ordered State Department letters back to Times New Roman. A roadside printer is copying him, binning Calibri leaflets before the community lunch. Volunteers need some food and help shifting the bins. The shredder has agreed to accept both sides.
Share some food; haul the bins → You share lunch and haul the bins, back aching. The leaflets say exactly the same thing. American diplomacy has simply decided the letters need feet.
Photograph the font purge → You photograph both versions and Rubio’s order. Every sentence survives. The nation’s dignity apparently rests on tiny legs underneath the alphabet.

Scene: The printer holds two unlettered sample sheets over overflowing recycling bins; a volunteer indicates bins awaiting movement. Travelers watch from the yard entrance. Identical-looking sheets have been separated into ceremonially opposed bins that empty into one shredder.
Editable overlays: “CALIBRI” — Blank card on left bin; “TIMES NEW ROMAN” — Blank card on right bin
Source: AP: Rubio orders return to Times New Roman (2025-12-10)
ENC-C02-A · Supporting dinner
At a pantry preparing for the 2025 SNAP cuts, volunteers welcome your hungry crew and any help you can spare. A senator’s tax-cut leaflet props up the short table leg. It’s finally supporting dinner.
Eat; take some food → You eat and take some food. The tax-cut leaflet stays under the table; removing it would cost everyone their lunch.
Record the volunteers’ account → You record the volunteers and collect some food. They ask you to include the casserole before Washington counts it as unnecessary spending.
Donate some food → You donate some food. A volunteer tapes your receipt over the senator’s smile. The first thing on that leaflet that fed anyone.

Scene: The cook offers empty plates while a volunteer indicates the food available for travelers and the donation table. A glossy politician leaflet is folded under a short table leg supporting the serving dishes.
Editable overlays: “TAX CUTS” — Blank folded leaflet beneath the table leg
Source: 2025 reconciliation law contains SNAP spending reductions and eligibility changes alongside tax provisions. Describe the law/fo…
ENC-C02-B · Proof of lunch

Your crew is welcomed at a supper for workers untangling the expanded SNAP work rules. A cleaner’s proof of employment occupies the only chair she hasn’t cleaned. Volunteers are collecting their accounts for D.C.
Eat; take some food → You eat and collect some food. The cleaner puts her payslips under a plate. For once, they help her keep a meal.
Record the cleaner’s account → You record her account and take some food. She clocks the interview. Even explaining she’s employed is becoming a second job.
Add some food to supper → You add some food. Volunteers record the donation on one line; nobody needs your manager to confirm you were holding the tin.

Scene: A cleaner gathers her blank payslip sheets from a chair while a volunteer offers the arriving travelers a place at supper. A stack of employment paperwork has its own place at the table while its owner stands.
Editable overlays: “PROOF OF WORK” — Editable heading above the blank paperwork tray
Source: 2025 reconciliation law expands SNAP requirements and creates Medicaid community-engagement requirements. Medicaid federal roll…
ENC-C02-C · Speech with gravy

A kitchen near the highway is feeding travelers with leftovers from a super-PAC donor dinner. Your hungry crew is welcome to eat or help. The invitation promised unlimited political speech. Most of it was steak.
Eat; take some food → You eat and take some food. A steak finally meets someone who wasn’t charged admission to a constitutional right.
Record the cooks’ account → You record the leftovers and collect some food. The cooks cleared in three minutes what donors spent four hours calling speech.
Donate some food → You donate some food. The cook adds it to the pot without checking how loudly your bank account can talk.

Scene: The cook opens a catering tray while travelers consider the offered meal; the donation table remains untouched by the crew. Ornate donor place cards surround enormous leftover steaks above ordinary chipped plates.
Editable overlays: “UNLIMITED SPEECH” — Blank donor invitation propped beside the catering tray
Source: Citizens United and SpeechNow underpin unlimited independent spending and contributions to independent-expenditure-only committ…
ENC-C03-A · Closing-time education

Trump ordered steps toward closing the Education Department. At a PTA fundraiser, parents ask your stopped crew to feed the volunteers or record their mock clearance sale. A desk is labelled “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS.” Two parents are arguing over how to lift it.
Share some food; join the sale → You share some food and join the parents’ mock auction. The desk goes to whoever can explain long division without crying.
Record the parents’ display → You record the display for D.C. The chair marked “local control” still has a federal assembly diagram taped underneath.
Provision the quiet reading corner → You leave some supplies and settle into the reading corner. The book opens without anyone first abolishing its publisher.
Scene: Parents examine a heavy desk while volunteers invite the travelers toward the food and recording tables. Two parents study opposite ends of a large desk supposedly transferring power to them.
Editable overlays: “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS” — Blank desk sale tag
Source: March 2025 EO directs the secretary to facilitate closure to extent permitted by law. Do not claim Congress actually abolished …
ENC-C03-B · The dry wing

Trump announced a donor-funded White House ballroom because big dinners needed tents. At a roadside social club, members hold a benefit under a leaking marquee. Bring some food and you may name the grand new wing. It’s the dry corner.
Share some food; name the new wing → You donate some food and name the dry corner after yourself. Someone moves a folding chair into it. Your presidential legacy seats one.
Record the ballroom comparison → You record the announcement and the club’s budget. Trump’s donors buy a ballroom. These donors can currently afford the word ballroom.
Supply the quiet picnic corner → You donate supplies and sit quietly. The club names the napkin holder after you. Donor access is very affordable without a president attached.

Scene: A member points at the single dry corner while another holds a food-donation bowl; travelers stand outside the tent considering the invitation. An elaborate ribbon encloses one dry folding chair while rain drips into cooking pots elsewhere.
Editable overlays: “NAME THE NEW WING” — Blank benefit placard
Source: White House announces ballroom construction (2025-07-31)
ENC-C03-C · Your call is a commitment

A court threw out the FTC’s click-to-cancel rule. At a roadside potluck, a neighbor is trying to cancel his gym membership on speakerphone. He invites you to bring some food or use the quiet room. The hold music has outlasted two casseroles.
Share some food; join the exercise → You share some food and cheer him on. The gym offers three free months. He asks whether any of them include leaving.
Record his cancellation attempt → With his permission, you record him selecting cancellation. A voice congratulates him on choosing continued membership. Nobody touches the phone for a moment.
Supply the quiet room → You donate some supplies and settle in the quiet room. Its door opens from inside. You consider recommending it to the gym.

Scene: The driver holds his phone over the table while a host indicates the food table and open quiet-room door; travelers consider the invitation. Two nearly empty casserole dishes flank a phone still playing hold music, with a fresh casserole waiting behind them.
Editable overlays: “PLEASE CONTINUE HOLDING” — Editable caption above the blank phone screen
Source: AP: Appeals court vacates FTC click-to-cancel rule (2025-07-09)
ENC-C04-A · Ground contact

NASA says Athena’s sideways landing left its drill unable to reach the Moon. At a roadside astronomy picnic, volunteers need help with a homemade lander display. Their drill has already completed the ground-contact phase.
Help haul the lander platform → You haul the platform until your shoulders ache. The picnic cheers its successful landing on the far side of the table.
Donate materials for the display → Your supplies secure the platform, earning the volunteers’ endorsement. Their procurement program now includes checking which way is up.
Record the actual mission result → You record the drill’s failure and the instruments that returned data. The volunteer retires a much simpler, less accurate disaster joke.
Scene: A volunteer indicates a homemade lander platform awaiting help, with a hand drill resting beside it. A modest drill bit already touches the picnic table beneath a tilted lunar-lander model.
Source: NASA Planetary Data System: CLPS TO PRIME-1 Athena (2025-03-06)
Source: NASA Intuitive Machines CLPS mission press kit
ENC-C04-B · Domestic adjectives

The FTC accused patriotic-goods sellers of false Made in USA claims and proposed a settlement. At a hardware shop, a worker is rebuilding a returned flag-display stand and invites help or materials. The advertising arrived entirely American. Several components apparently took a longer route.
Help haul the display sections → You haul the sections until your shoulders ache and enjoy the company. The flag needs a sturdy base more than another adjective.
Donate repair materials → Your materials secure the stand and earn trust. The worker records their actual source, an unexpectedly radical approach to product description.
Record the origin-claim distinction → You record the allegation and proposed settlement accurately. The worker removes an unsupported claim without needing to lower the flag.

Scene: A worker offers help with a stationary disassembled display stand beside unopened repair materials. A lavish blank patriotic product sleeve surrounds a pile of visibly mismatched ordinary components.
Source: FTC Announces Made in the USA Sweep (2026-04-14)
Source: Americana Liberty FTC case timeline: April 14, 2026
ENC-C04-C · Freedom from shade

At a travelling workers’ fair, Florida roofers show your crew the law blocking local heat protections. Their protest canopy covers the water cooler. A sponsor praising deregulation has put his chair underneath it. The roofers need help moving the display.
Help move the demonstration canopy → You haul the canopy until your arms ache. The roofers laugh as the sponsor follows its shadow without once supporting the policy.
Donate some water for workers → You donate some water; the roofers record your help. The sponsor calls hydration a personal responsibility, then asks whose cooler this is.
Record the roofers’ demonstration → You record the roofers explaining the Florida law. The sponsor keeps edging into the shot, specifically the shaded part.
Scene: Roofers point to a canopy awaiting repositioning while a sponsor sits beneath it and travelers watch. The anti-regulation sponsor's chair monopolizes the shade around the workers' cooler.
Editable overlays: “LOCAL HEAT RULES BLOCKED” — Blank display panel beside the canopy
Source: DeSantis signed Florida 2024 law barring local government heat/water-break mandates. This does not make drinking water illegal …
ENC-C05-A · Return to nonexistent sender

At a library stop, volunteers give your crew letters about the nonexistent studies in the first MAHA report. They offer some food for an accurate recorded reply. A retired postman has brought an empty envelope. “That’s all the research we could fit.”
Read and save the letters → You read and save the letters, laughing. The postman has underlined “address unknown” so hard the nonexistent study now has a window.
Record an accurate reply → You record the citation corrections and collect some food. The librarian checks the reply exists before pressing play.
Share some food; sort letters → You share some food and sort the letters with the volunteers. Every missing study gets a real paperclip. The science budget is recovering.

Scene: A retired postman holds an empty envelope open while a volunteer shows the travelers letters and available food. The prominently held envelope contains absolutely nothing; large stacks of actual correspondence surround it.
Editable overlays: “ADDRESS UNKNOWN” — Blank envelope front
Source: May 2025 reporting identified nonexistent studies and other citation problems in the initial MAHA report. HHS said citation and…
ENC-C05-B · Too big for the form

A community volunteer flags down your van with letters about the Pentagon accepting Qatar’s luxury jet. Her workplace made her declare a gifted muffin. She offers some food for a recorded reply. Her copy of the form asks whether the muffin has foreign owners.
Read and save the letters → You save the letters and laugh over the muffin declaration. The volunteer drew landing gear underneath it. Compliance rejected the extra wheels.
Record an accurate reply → You record the jet acceptance and collect some food. She declares the sandwiches herself. “No wings. We should be all right.”
Share some food; sort letters → You share some food and help sort letters. Someone folds the muffin form into an aircraft. Its gift exemption improves immediately.
Scene: A volunteer displays a blank gift form beside a plain muffin and gestures to letters for the crew. The modest muffin is surrounded by oversized paperwork and a small paper airplane.
Editable overlays: “GIFT DECLARATION” — Blank heading area on the muffin form
Source: The Pentagon announced on May 21, 2025 that it had accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar for presidential use. Acceptance prompted l…
ENC-C05-C · The other dinner guests

After Trump’s dinner for top meme-coin investors, diner regulars have written their own requests for a hearing. They flag down your crew to carry them to D.C. The cook offers some food for a recorded reply. Their invitation is clipped to an unpaid gas bill.
Read and save their letters → You save the letters, laughing at the guest list. Occupation: dishwasher. Investment portfolio: a glove containing enough quarters for the laundry.
Record an accurate reply → You record their requests and collect some food. The cook announces the exclusive reception. It’s behind the counter, beside the mop.
Share some food; sort requests → You share some food and sort the requests. The regulars toast your arrival with tap water. Nobody checks its market capitalization.

Scene: Regulars show the travelers their invitation and blank letters while the cook indicates food available for the road. An elaborate homemade invitation is clipped to an ordinary unpaid bill beside a glove full of coins.
Editable overlays: “REQUEST FOR A HEARING” — Blank invitation panel
Source: Trump hosted top investors in his meme coin at his Virginia golf club on May 22, 2025; roughly 220 were invited. This establish…
ENC-C06-A · The coverage ladder

At a health-funding teach-in, volunteers show your stopped crew how the 2025 Medicaid law changes eligibility and spending. They’ve built a demonstration ladder. The bottom rung is labelled “taxpayer.” The first reachable rung has been removed to keep the model affordable.
Check the law and demonstration → You check the sources and understand the changes. The volunteer restores the missing rung for packing. Even the demonstration needs it to work.
Watch the volunteers rehearse → You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer playing a senator praises the ladder from a stepladder somebody else brought.
Scene: Volunteers point to the missing rung of an unoccupied display ladder while travelers observe. A separate sturdy stepladder stands behind the person praising the damaged model.
Editable overlays: “TAXPAYER” — Blank tag attached to bottom ladder support
Source: P.L.119-21 reduces projected federal Medicaid spending and changes eligibility. Projected insurance losses are projections, not…
ENC-C06-B · Priced by the department

Washington offered federal agencies Musk’s Grok AI for forty-two cents. At a roadside job fair, a host rehearses interviews with a talking toy and invites you to try. He asks whether human wages can also cover an entire department.
Check what the bargain actually buys → You explain the agency-access price, gaining trust and clarity. The host restores the wage column. The toy remains available at wholesale.
Try the practice interview → You quote your salary per entire department. The group laughs; the host admits that one person still expects one actual paycheck.

Scene: A host presents a talking toy beside a blank job board and invites the waiting travelers toward an empty interview chair. The tiny talking toy sits behind an enormous desk while the human interview chair is a folding stool.
Source: GSA and xAI Partner on $0.42 per Agency Agreement to Accelerate Federal AI Adoption (2025-09-25)
ENC-C06-C · The secondary title

Trump authorized “Department of War” as a secondary title. At a veterans’ hall stop, volunteers invite your crew to inspect their proposed response: rename the leaky roof “Air Superiority.” A bucket already controls the space beneath it.
Record the proposal and leak → You check the naming announcement and record the hall’s response. The veteran tips out the bucket. Air superiority has reached the carpet.
Join the naming rehearsal → You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer christens the mop “Strategic Deterrence.” The leak starts another drop while he’s still saluting.
Scene: Volunteers show a proposed blank roof-name card while a bucket catches an existing leak and travelers watch. A humble bucket occupies the exact territory claimed by an ambitious new title.
Editable overlays: “AIR SUPERIORITY” — Blank proposed name card beside the bucket
Source: September 2025 action authorized Department of War as a secondary title. Do not claim Congress abolished the statutory Departme…
ENC-C07-A · The peace division

FIFA gave Trump its first peace prize. A trophy repairer is adding a peace division between bowling and darts. He offers $10 and some food for lifting the display; repair materials and lunch company are welcome. The new department still needs shelf brackets.
Donate some repair materials → Your materials earn the repairer’s endorsement. The peace division acquires the modest structural support unavailable from an acceptance speech.
Lift the display for $10 and food → You earn cash, food, and sore muscles, laughing as world peace takes its place between a bowling ball and crossed darts.
Share food; record the award’s origin → You share lunch and record that FIFA created its own prize. The repairer keeps the Nobel label in a different drawer.

Scene: A repairer indicates a stationary trophy display and loose shelf brackets between bowling and dart trophies. A newly polished peace-themed cup has nowhere to stand between two crowded sports shelves.
Source: FIFA: President Donald J. Trump awarded inaugural FIFA Peace Prize (2025-12-05)
ENC-C07-B · Returned to the parents

Trump’s order to facilitate closing the Education Department has inspired a PTA’s “do it ourselves” fundraiser. They offer your stopped crew $10 and some food to shift donated desks. The volunteers have received local control. It came without a furniture dolly.
Donate supplies for the fundraiser → You donate some supplies; the PTA records your help. A parent attaches felt feet to a desk. Local control stops scratching the floor.
Take the desk-moving job → You earn $10 and some food with an aching back. A parent applauds. “Excellent. You’re now qualified to run the furniture department.”
Share some food; record concerns → You share some food and record the parents’ questions. They want to know which part of closing a department makes the desk lighter.
Scene: Parents assess desks awaiting relocation and show the travelers a blank job board. A large stack of desks sits beside a conspicuously absent dolly, represented only by an empty storage hook.
Editable overlays: “DESK MOVING: $10 + FOOD” — Blank job-offer board
Source: March 2025 EO directs the secretary to facilitate closure to extent permitted by law. Do not claim Congress actually abolished …
ENC-C07-C · Apparently overhead

At a research fundraiser opposing the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap, volunteers offer your crew $10 and some food to shift equipment. They also need supplies. The display labels the freezer “overhead.” A scientist is demonstrating what happens when overhead melts onto your shoes.
Donate supplies to the display → You donate some supplies; volunteers record your contribution. The scientist finally puts the thawing demonstration in a tray. Waste has stopped leaking.
Take the equipment-moving job → You earn $10 and some food, arms aching. Moving the empty freezer proves overhead weighs considerably more than the speech against it.
Share some food; record testimony → You share some food and record the scientist’s concerns. She points at the freezer plug. “The breakthrough is inside. It needs electricity.”

Scene: A scientist points to a tray beneath a safe demonstration freezer while volunteers offer the travelers a moving job. A freezer classified as overhead stands above a puddle from melting demonstration ice.
Editable overlays: “OVERHEAD • MOVING WORK $10 + FOOD” — Blank display board beside the empty freezer
Source: UT Southwestern estimated in February 2025 that the proposed cap risked over 100m yearly. Do not present the estimate or propos…
ENC-C08-A · Patriotic cartography

Trump’s Gulf renaming has left a roadside map club with old charts and new federal labels. They ask your stopped crew to help prepare a public comparison. The volunteer has carefully checked the coast. It has made no effort to move.
Donate supplies for comparison charts → You donate some supplies and help document the labels. The volunteer uses a ruler to confirm that greatness added no coastline.
Share some food with the club → You share some food, and everyone invents patriotic names for the crumbs. The plate becomes the first disputed territory to disappear.
Check and save the charts → You compare and save the charts, relieved to find the coordinates unchanged. The volunteer gives the compass permission to remain neutral.
Scene: A volunteer aligns two matching blank coast charts while travelers consider helping. Both charts share precisely the same shoreline beneath differently positioned blank title cards.
Editable overlays: “SAME COAST. NEW FEDERAL NAME.” — Editable header above the two blank charts
Source: January 2025 EO directed federal use of Gulf of America and restoration of Mount McKinley naming; it did not change geography o…
ENC-C08-B · A place at the table

Inspired by Trump’s dinner for top meme-coin investors, residents at a roadside café are preparing an access-to-government display. They ask your crew for help. A place setting for an ordinary voter includes a folding chair outside the window.
Donate supplies for the display → You donate some supplies and help document the display. The volunteer moves the voter’s chair closer. It can now smell access.
Share some food; join the rehearsal → You share some food and rehearse the voter’s dinner. Everyone laughs when the server presents the menu through binoculars.
Check and save the dinner report → You check and save the report about the investor dinner. The café owner unlocks the outside chair. “No minimum holding here.”
Scene: A volunteer arranges an unoccupied folding chair outside the window opposite an ornate table inside. The ordinary voter's empty place is outside, facing an elaborate indoor dinner table.
Editable overlays: “ORDINARY VOTER” — Blank place card on the outside chair
Source: Trump hosted top investors in his meme coin at his Virginia golf club on May 22, 2025; roughly 220 were invited. This establish…
ENC-C08-C · Royal toll exemption

Trump tried to end New York’s congestion toll and posted “Long Live the King.” A judge blocked the attempt. At a carpool picnic, a visiting New York courier shows his bill. Hosts invite supplies for recording drivers’ accounts, or some food to share. His bill accepts money, not royal proclamations.

Donate supplies to record drivers’ accounts → You donate supplies and preserve the accounts. The courier attaches the presidential post to his toll bill. They disagree about who is running the kingdom.
Share some food; hear the courier’s story → You share some food and hear his story. “I tried saying Long Live the King at the toll bill,” he says. “Turns out it wanted Long Live My Debit Card.”
Compare and save the toll maps → You save the old and current toll maps and make sense of the ruling. The courier puts away his toy crown. The border of Manhattan remains unmoved by headwear.

Scene: The courier displays a toll bill beside two maps while the host indicates the donation table; travelers stand listening. A toy crown sits beside a toll bill that continues to look completely ordinary and payable.
Editable overlays: “LONG LIVE THE KING” — Editable caption on a blank printout of the documented post
Source: New York governor’s transcript on the federal congestion-pricing reversal attempt (2025-02-19)
Source: Southern District of New York: Congestion-pricing opinion (2026-03-03)
ENC-C09-A · Delivered, according to the calendar

USPS changed delivery targets in 2025: some faster, some slower. At a picnic beside the post office, a retired carrier offers his new guide and some food for hauling display boards. His birthday card says “Sorry I’m late” in pencil. He’s waiting for the target to decide.
Record the carrier’s guide → You save the guide with the USPS announcement. He erases “late” from the card. The envelope hasn’t moved, but its performance has improved.
Haul the boards for some food → You earn some food and a sore shoulder. He calls it same-day delivery. You ask him not to tell management what they can get for a sandwich.
Listen to the carrier’s tour → He walks you through the changed targets. Then he opens the card: “Happy birthday, approximately.” You laugh hard enough to need the picnic bench.

Scene: The carrier holds a birthday card and pencil beside two unopened display boards; the organizer indicates the work and waiting food. Travelers listen without moving anything. A birthday cake sits under a cover while its unsent card waits beside an eraser as though the calendar may excuse it.
Editable overlays: “SORRY I’M LATE” — Editable text on the blank birthday card
Source: USPS announces refined service standards and cost reductions (2025-02-26)
ENC-C09-B · Still employed by the tower

Transportation Secretary Duffy told Congress in July 2025 that parts of air-traffic infrastructure still used floppy disks. At an electronics recycler, a worker offers food for hauling stock. He nearly recycled one of those disks. Apparently it still has a federal day job.
Record what the testimony actually said → You record the limited infrastructure claim and earn trust. The worker keeps one obsolete disk out of the box marked by age alone.
Haul the stock for some food → You earn food and sore muscles. Yesterday’s home-computer junk travels across the yard with more ceremony than it expected.
Hear the recycler’s sales pitch → His pitch cheers you up: vintage storage, mature technology, references available from Congress. He almost sounds like a procurement brochure.

Scene: A worker holds a floppy disk above an unopened scrap carton and offers a stock-hauling job. A tiny floppy disk receives a pristine display cushion while larger old computers wait in battered boxes.
Source: Secretary Duffy: July 2025 transportation oversight testimony (2025-07-16)
ENC-C09-C · Messages for the public

A library’s public security demonstration follows the Trump officials’ Signal leak. They invite your stopped crew to record it, or shift cabinets for some food. The librarian has placed the public-comment box inside a safe. “We can’t get anything into their chat.”
Record the security demonstration → You record the demonstration accurately. The librarian opens the safe for a comment about potholes. It needs more steps than joining that chat.
Shift cabinets for some food → You move cabinets until your back aches and collect some food. Public opinion is now secure against anyone attempting to hear it.
Watch the comment-box demonstration → You laugh when the librarian tries feeding the safe a postcard. It accepts national-security concerns but jams on a missing bus shelter.

Scene: A librarian shows a safe containing an empty public-comment box while travelers consider the work and demonstration. The humble comment box has conspicuously excessive security compared with a plain phone on the table.
Editable overlays: “PUBLIC COMMENTS” — Blank card visible on the box inside the open safe
Source: In March 2025 senior Trump officials shared Yemen strike details in a Signal chat that accidentally included a journalist. Fict…
ENC-C10-A · Customers sold separately

The FTC’s rule bars fabricated consumer reviews. A café’s opening party has a practical problem: its marketing contractor invented the delighted diners, then ordered chairs for them. The owner asks you to record the mismatch or help move the furniture. The reviews require less seating.
Record the empty-seat comparison → You record what you actually see and earn trust. The invented diners remain enthusiastic, punctual, and remarkably easy to interview simultaneously.
Help push the chair trolley outside → You strain your muscles and enjoy the ridiculous procession. A whole crowd of imaginary customers leaves without anyone needing a doggy bag.
Scene: An owner gestures between rows of empty chairs and a loaded, stationary chair trolley. A grand opening arrangement has lavish seating and no arriving diners.
Source: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule: Questions and Answers (2024-10-21)
ENC-C10-B · The shrinking bed

Nurses at a roadside fundraiser demonstrate the 2025 law’s projected Medicaid cuts with an adjustable display bed. They ask your crew to add testimony or move it. A volunteer shortens the mattress while keeping the pillow labelled “patient choice” impressively plump.
Add testimony to the nurses’ record → You add your experience to the nurses’ record. The volunteer asks whether you prefer your feet or head outside the model’s coverage.
Help move the demonstration bed → You haul the bed until your arms ache. Everyone laughs when the pillow slides off. Patient choice has left the building first.
Scene: A nurse adjusts an empty display bed while another indicates the route it will later be moved. A comically plump pillow overwhelms a visibly shortened demonstration mattress.
Editable overlays: “PATIENT CHOICE” — Blank pillow tag
Source: P.L.119-21 reduces projected federal Medicaid spending and changes eligibility. Projected insurance losses are projections, not…
ENC-C10-C · Please declare your aircraft

Workers protesting their employer’s no-tip rule have built a cardboard jet after the Pentagon accepted Qatar’s plane. They flag your crew down for testimony or a hand pushing it. The wings are made from rejected gift declarations. One used to be about a biscuit.
Record the workers’ account → You record the employer’s rule and the workers’ account. The biscuit declaration includes its approximate value. Nobody has filled in cruising altitude.
Help push the cardboard jet → You push until your shoulder aches and the crowd cheers. A tip jar rolls down the runway in business class.
Scene: Workers display a stationary cardboard aircraft assembled from blank forms and invite the travelers to help. An ordinary tip jar sits in the cardboard jet's otherwise elaborate front cabin.
Editable overlays: “GIFT DECLARATION” — Editable label over the blank wing forms
Source: The Pentagon announced on May 21, 2025 that it had accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar for presidential use. Acceptance prompted l…
ENC-C11-A · The cost of the plug

Your crew stops at a public briefing on the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap. A researcher has brought itemized costs, chairs, and an unplugged freezer to explain what “overhead” pays for. The demonstration ice is providing a floor-level impact assessment.
Check the cost breakdown → You verify the figures with a headache. The researcher adds electricity to the example. The ice has already submitted its objection.
Sit while the researcher presents → You sit and ease your sore legs. The researcher quietly plugs in a fan. Overhead immediately improves conditions for the taxpayer.
Save the researcher’s sourced estimate → You save the dated estimate and its proposal status. The researcher sets the papers above the puddle. That shelf is overhead too.

Scene: A researcher shows cost sheets beside safe demonstration equipment; empty chairs are available to the watching travelers. Demonstration ice drips beneath an unplugged freezer while a plugged-in fan waits nearby.
Editable overlays: “OVERHEAD” — Blank board beside the demonstration freezer
Source: UT Southwestern estimated in February 2025 that the proposed cap risked over 100m yearly. Do not present the estimate or propos…
ENC-C11-B · The passport objection

At an airport print kiosk, an attendant’s demonstration distinguishes REAL ID from other acceptable identification. TSA’s $45 ConfirmID option is for travelers lacking acceptable ID, not everyone without REAL ID. A passport keeps interrupting the expensive version of the story.
Check the demonstration’s examples → You check the examples through tired eyes and earn trust. The passport succeeds without being promoted into a state driver’s license.
Sit through the short demonstration → You sit and recover while the attendant explains accepted IDs. The chair conducts no additional verification of its occupant.
Save the accepted-ID distinction → You save the official distinction accurately. The attendant sets the passport beside the fee notice, giving the expensive misunderstanding a proper rival.

Outside a coffee kiosk, a worker shows you the SEC’s Keurig case: recyclability reports omitted major recyclers’ objections. She is checking the kiosk’s local collection rules over lunch. The annual report seems much easier to recycle than the coffee pod.
Share some food with the worker → You share lunch and exchange numbers. She finishes her coffee, then checks the real bin instructions instead of consulting investor relations.
Compare the SEC finding with the claims → You save a careful account through tired eyes. The report’s missing qualification turns out to be most of the practical question.
Leave the kiosk → You leave frustrated. The worker holds the pod over two bins while the corporate report enjoys several confident paragraphs.

Scene: A worker compares a blank report with a blank local collection guide while holding an unused pod above the counter. The report is poised neatly over the recycling bin while the pod remains undecided between two bins.
Source: SEC Charges Keurig with Inaccurate Statements Regarding K-Cup Recyclability (2024-09-10)
ENC-W-PC-C02-B · Bill the person who hired you

A New York transplant waits outside a moving-supply shop, laughing at an old broker invoice. New York City’s FARE Act makes landlord-hired brokers charge their employer, not the tenant. She welcomes lunch company. The bill has finally learned who ordered it.
Share some food with the mover → You share lunch and exchange numbers. She turns the old invoice toward the landlord’s address, giving it useful moving directions.
Compare the invoice with the city rule → You preserve the landlord-hired distinction through tired eyes. The broker’s work can still cost money; she just did not hire that broker.
Return to the van → You leave annoyed. She packs the invoice separately from her belongings. It has spent enough time trying to move in with her.

Scene: A mover holds an old blank invoice beside unopened moving boxes and an untouched lunch. A bill-shaped envelope tries to occupy its own oversized moving box among the mover’s modest possessions.
Source: DCWP: The FARE Act Is Now in Effect (2025-06-11)
ENC-W-PC-C02-C · The shareholder needs changing

Trump Accounts give eligible newborns $1,000 invested, with ordinary withdrawals locked until the year they turn eighteen. At a coastal grocery, a parent needs diapers today. A promoter waves the brochure. The baby has already begun distributing something.
Share supplies with the parent → You share supplies and exchange numbers. The promoter calls this an excellent investment; the parent hands him the used diaper.
Read the withdrawal rules → You save the restriction through a headache. The brochure’s smiling baby has eighteen years of diapers missing from its financial plan.
Return to the van → You leave dispirited. The promoter keeps saying compounding while the parent searches for somewhere flat to deal with what is compounding.
Scene: Parent indicates diaper shelf; promoter holds an unopened brochure; crew considers the situation. A grand investment display towers over an urgently needed diaper.
Editable overlays: “$1,000 FOR ELIGIBLE NEWBORNS” — promotion header; “ORDINARY WITHDRAWALS: YEAR CHILD TURNS 18” — brochure callout; “DIAPERS” — shelf overlay
Source: Eligible US-citizen children born in 2025-2028 can receive a $1000 pilot contribution in a Trump Account. Ordinary distribution…
ENC-W-SW-C01-A · Freedom is leaking under the door

Trump ordered showerhead deregulation in the name of freedom. At a desert motel, the owner demonstrates his new attachment and offers $12 to move wet linen bins. Water spreads under the bathroom door. He proudly calls it government getting out of the way.
Move the linen bins for $12 → You earn $12 and sore muscles. Government is out of the way; you are now standing in it up to the ankles.
Buy food and water for $6 → You buy supplies for $6. The owner warns you not to waste the bottled water while his liberated bathroom enters the hallway.
Compare the claim with the plumbing → You document the demonstration through a headache. The freedom announcement is laminated; the towel budget was less prepared.
Scene: Owner points to untouched linen bins as demonstration water creeps under a closed bathroom door. The owner holds a pristine laminated freedom announcement above spreading water.
Editable overlays: “FREEDOM FLOWS” — demonstration card; “$12 linen-moving job” — offer card; “$6 food + water” — reception card
Source: April 2025 Executive Order 14264 directed rescission of the 2021 showerhead definition; it framed the action as restoring freed…
ENC-W-SW-C01-B · The straw gets a security detail

Trump ordered federal agencies to stop buying paper straws. At a desert fair, a booster has put one in a locked evidence case. A contractor offers $12 to move water crates. The cups are empty; the dangerous straw has its own spotlight.
Move the water crates for $12 → You earn $12 and sore arms. The booster asks you to keep condensation away from the straw until the photographer arrives.
Buy food and water for $6 → You buy supplies for $6. A volunteer offers a plastic straw so you can hydrate in a manner acceptable to the display.
Read the order beside the display → You document the spectacle through a headache. Federal procurement has become a desert hostage scene with a drinking tube under glass.
Scene: Contractor points to sealed water crates while booster guards a straw under a blank glass display. A single straw receives theatrical protection beside an empty cup stack and untouched water.
Editable overlays: “PAPER STRAW EVIDENCE” — case placard; “$12 crate-moving job” — offer card; “$6 food + water” — counter card
Source: February 2025 order directed agencies to end paper-straw procurement and develop a broader strategy. It did not prohibit custom…
ENC-W-SW-C01-C · Destination pending government

After a court blocked the administration’s 2026 FBI headquarters move, a freight clerk keeps two destinations on his planning board. He offers $12 to move water crates; food and water cost $6. Your purchase can travel farther with a simpler address: the van outside.
Carry the water crates for $12 → You earn $12 and sore muscles. The crates reach their destination without a revised federal real-estate announcement.
Buy food and water for $6 → You buy food and water. The clerk watches them reach the van, visibly enjoying a headquarters decision that sticks.
Compare the announcement with the court decision → You save the blocked-move distinction through tired eyes. The clerk removes a delivery date the announcement never had authority to guarantee.

Scene: A clerk indicates unopened water crates beside a planning board with two opposing blank destination arrows. The elaborate two-arrow plan sits behind a simple clear path from the food counter to the parked van.
Source: Maryland Attorney General Statement on FBI Headquarters Ruling (2026-08-17)
Source: AP reporting on court blocking FBI headquarters move
Source: FBI: New FBI Headquarters in Washington, DC
ENC-W-SW-C02-A · The other barrier

NIH ended the embargo for covered new research manuscripts in July 2025. A library porter offers food for carrying printed copies, or $10 to match delivery slips. The publisher’s barrier has gone. The doorway remains annoyingly narrow, and these boxes will not download themselves inside.
Carry the boxes for some food → You earn food and aching muscles. The research reaches its readers after passing the last obstacle: a door designed before anyone measured the boxes.
Match the delivery slips for $10 → You earn $10 and the porter’s endorsement, eyes aching. Every reader gets the right public manuscript without purchasing the privilege of knowing it exists.
Pass on the work → You leave disappointed. The porter turns a box sideways, making a small practical improvement in public access.
Scene: A porter indicates unopened paper boxes wider than a narrow doorway and unmatched blank delivery slips. The now-accessible research is physically stopped by an ordinary narrow doorway.
Source: NIH Public Access Policy Overview (2025-07-01)
Source: NIH Notice: Accelerated Implementation of 2024 Public Access Policy
ENC-W-SW-C02-B · Express delivery, eventually

Trump directed the FAA to replace the overland supersonic ban with noise-based rules. A roadside caterer offers food for loading lunch crates, or $10 to check delivery slips. She likes the faster-than-sound ambition. Her van is still behind a tractor.
Load the lunch crates for food → You earn food and sore muscles. Every crate reaches the van below the speed of sound, with lunch inside it.
Check the delivery slips for $10 → You earn $10 and an endorsement through tired eyes. The slips promise addresses, which remain more useful than promised future airspeed.
Pass on the work → You leave disappointed. The caterer watches the tractor advance another yard, implementing its own gradual transition to faster travel.

Scene: A caterer offers work beside unloaded lunch crates while a tractor blocks the lane beyond the parked catering van. A sleek blank model jet sits on the dashboard of a van stuck behind a bulky tractor.
Source: Executive Order 14304: Leading the World in Supersonic Flight (2025-06-06)
ENC-W-SW-C02-C · Equipment appreciation day

Texas exempts qualifying business property worth up to $125,000 per taxing unit. At an independent produce depot, the owner frames the notice beside his labeling machine. He offers some food for boxing produce or $10 to sort dispatch labels. “Hard work finally recognized,” he says, polishing the machine.
Box produce for food → You earn some food and an aching back. He poses the machine for a thank-you picture. You move the boxes out of its light.
Sort dispatch labels for $10 → You earn $10, save the exemption notice and rest your aching eyes. Your payment gets a receipt. The machine’s tax break gets a frame.
Decline the shift → You leave frustrated. He studies an empty crate to see whether it counts as exempt business property. It’s the first box he’s handled all afternoon.

Scene: The owner polishes a labeling machine beneath a blank framed notice while a worker indicates empty boxes and unsorted dispatch labels; travelers consider the offers. An idle machine receives a framed tribute while the human work waits beside it without ceremony.
Editable overlays: “BUSINESS PROPERTY EXEMPTION” — Editable heading on the blank framed notice; “$10: SORT DISPATCH LABELS” — Blank work offer
Source: Texas Comptroller: Valuing property and business personal property exemption (Current 2026 guidance checked 2026-09-14)

72 draft packages. Images have no embedded text; wording listed as an overlay is rendered separately.
ENC-C01-A · Smaller government
DOGE fired the park’s cleaners. The remaining ranger hasn’t had lunch. She offers your crew gloves beside overflowing bins. “Congratulations. You’re the smaller government.”
Share some food and help clear the bins → You share lunch and haul bags until your back aches. She hands you a bin liner. “Uniform allowance.”
Photograph the mess for your D.C. case → You photograph the overflowing bins. She points at the flies. “Only department still recruiting.”
Scene: A tired ranger offers unused gloves toward the watching travelers; nobody has accepted them. Overflowing bins crowd out the picnic furniture; flies hover over the only busy department.
Source: The administration fired about 1000 newly hired NPS staff in February 2025, including maintenance and cleaning roles. Do not pr…
ENC-C01-B · Permission to spin
At a roadside repair co-op, a mechanic shows you Oregon’s law limiting software locks on spare parts. Volunteers need some food and help salvaging switches. A washing machine rejects a working replacement. It accepts dirty underwear without checking the manufacturer.
Share some food; salvage switches → You share lunch and wrench out switches until your wrists ache. The drum can spin. The company’s permission is still buffering.
Photograph the lockout and Oregon law → You save the error and Oregon’s rule for D.C. The replacement fits perfectly. Ownership seems to be the incompatible part.
Scene: The mechanic holds a replacement switch beside an unlettered machine display while a volunteer indicates the unopened salvage bin; travelers consider helping. A machine full of mismatched socks accepts the laundry while its screen rejects the neatly fitting replacement control.
Editable overlays: “PART NOT RECOGNIZED” — Blank washing-machine display
Source: Oregon Revised Statutes: Right to Repair Consumer Equipment (2025 codification)
ENC-C01-C · Dignity, by the pound
Rubio ordered State Department letters back to Times New Roman. A roadside printer is copying him, binning Calibri leaflets before the community lunch. Volunteers need some food and help shifting the bins. The shredder has agreed to accept both sides.
Share some food; haul the bins → You share lunch and haul the bins, back aching. The leaflets say exactly the same thing. American diplomacy has simply decided the letters need feet.
Photograph the font purge → You photograph both versions and Rubio’s order. Every sentence survives. The nation’s dignity apparently rests on tiny legs underneath the alphabet.
Scene: The printer holds two unlettered sample sheets over overflowing recycling bins; a volunteer indicates bins awaiting movement. Travelers watch from the yard entrance. Identical-looking sheets have been separated into ceremonially opposed bins that empty into one shredder.
Editable overlays: “CALIBRI” — Blank card on left bin; “TIMES NEW ROMAN” — Blank card on right bin
Source: AP: Rubio orders return to Times New Roman (2025-12-10)
ENC-C02-A · Supporting dinner
At a pantry preparing for the 2025 SNAP cuts, volunteers welcome your hungry crew and any help you can spare. A senator’s tax-cut leaflet props up the short table leg. It’s finally supporting dinner.
Eat; take some food → You eat and take some food. The tax-cut leaflet stays under the table; removing it would cost everyone their lunch.
Record the volunteers’ account → You record the volunteers and collect some food. They ask you to include the casserole before Washington counts it as unnecessary spending.
Donate some food → You donate some food. A volunteer tapes your receipt over the senator’s smile. The first thing on that leaflet that fed anyone.
Scene: The cook offers empty plates while a volunteer indicates the food available for travelers and the donation table. A glossy politician leaflet is folded under a short table leg supporting the serving dishes.
Editable overlays: “TAX CUTS” — Blank folded leaflet beneath the table leg
Source: 2025 reconciliation law contains SNAP spending reductions and eligibility changes alongside tax provisions. Describe the law/fo…
ENC-C02-B · Proof of lunch
Your crew is welcomed at a supper for workers untangling the expanded SNAP work rules. A cleaner’s proof of employment occupies the only chair she hasn’t cleaned. Volunteers are collecting their accounts for D.C.
Eat; take some food → You eat and collect some food. The cleaner puts her payslips under a plate. For once, they help her keep a meal.
Record the cleaner’s account → You record her account and take some food. She clocks the interview. Even explaining she’s employed is becoming a second job.
Add some food to supper → You add some food. Volunteers record the donation on one line; nobody needs your manager to confirm you were holding the tin.
Scene: A cleaner gathers her blank payslip sheets from a chair while a volunteer offers the arriving travelers a place at supper. A stack of employment paperwork has its own place at the table while its owner stands.
Editable overlays: “PROOF OF WORK” — Editable heading above the blank paperwork tray
Source: 2025 reconciliation law expands SNAP requirements and creates Medicaid community-engagement requirements. Medicaid federal roll…
ENC-C02-C · Speech with gravy
A kitchen near the highway is feeding travelers with leftovers from a super-PAC donor dinner. Your hungry crew is welcome to eat or help. The invitation promised unlimited political speech. Most of it was steak.
Eat; take some food → You eat and take some food. A steak finally meets someone who wasn’t charged admission to a constitutional right.
Record the cooks’ account → You record the leftovers and collect some food. The cooks cleared in three minutes what donors spent four hours calling speech.
Donate some food → You donate some food. The cook adds it to the pot without checking how loudly your bank account can talk.
Scene: The cook opens a catering tray while travelers consider the offered meal; the donation table remains untouched by the crew. Ornate donor place cards surround enormous leftover steaks above ordinary chipped plates.
Editable overlays: “UNLIMITED SPEECH” — Blank donor invitation propped beside the catering tray
Source: Citizens United and SpeechNow underpin unlimited independent spending and contributions to independent-expenditure-only committ…
ENC-C03-A · Closing-time education
Trump ordered steps toward closing the Education Department. At a PTA fundraiser, parents ask your stopped crew to feed the volunteers or record their mock clearance sale. A desk is labelled “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS.” Two parents are arguing over how to lift it.
Share some food; join the sale → You share some food and join the parents’ mock auction. The desk goes to whoever can explain long division without crying.
Record the parents’ display → You record the display for D.C. The chair marked “local control” still has a federal assembly diagram taped underneath.
Provision the quiet reading corner → You leave some supplies and settle into the reading corner. The book opens without anyone first abolishing its publisher.
Scene: Parents examine a heavy desk while volunteers invite the travelers toward the food and recording tables. Two parents study opposite ends of a large desk supposedly transferring power to them.
Editable overlays: “POWER RETURNED TO PARENTS” — Blank desk sale tag
Source: March 2025 EO directs the secretary to facilitate closure to extent permitted by law. Do not claim Congress actually abolished …
ENC-C03-B · The dry wing
Trump announced a donor-funded White House ballroom because big dinners needed tents. At a roadside social club, members hold a benefit under a leaking marquee. Bring some food and you may name the grand new wing. It’s the dry corner.
Share some food; name the new wing → You donate some food and name the dry corner after yourself. Someone moves a folding chair into it. Your presidential legacy seats one.
Record the ballroom comparison → You record the announcement and the club’s budget. Trump’s donors buy a ballroom. These donors can currently afford the word ballroom.
Supply the quiet picnic corner → You donate supplies and sit quietly. The club names the napkin holder after you. Donor access is very affordable without a president attached.
Scene: A member points at the single dry corner while another holds a food-donation bowl; travelers stand outside the tent considering the invitation. An elaborate ribbon encloses one dry folding chair while rain drips into cooking pots elsewhere.
Editable overlays: “NAME THE NEW WING” — Blank benefit placard
Source: White House announces ballroom construction (2025-07-31)
ENC-C03-C · Your call is a commitment
A court threw out the FTC’s click-to-cancel rule. At a roadside potluck, a neighbor is trying to cancel his gym membership on speakerphone. He invites you to bring some food or use the quiet room. The hold music has outlasted two casseroles.
Share some food; join the exercise → You share some food and cheer him on. The gym offers three free months. He asks whether any of them include leaving.
Record his cancellation attempt → With his permission, you record him selecting cancellation. A voice congratulates him on choosing continued membership. Nobody touches the phone for a moment.
Supply the quiet room → You donate some supplies and settle in the quiet room. Its door opens from inside. You consider recommending it to the gym.
Scene: The driver holds his phone over the table while a host indicates the food table and open quiet-room door; travelers consider the invitation. Two nearly empty casserole dishes flank a phone still playing hold music, with a fresh casserole waiting behind them.
Editable overlays: “PLEASE CONTINUE HOLDING” — Editable caption above the blank phone screen
Source: AP: Appeals court vacates FTC click-to-cancel rule (2025-07-09)
ENC-C04-A · Ground contact
NASA says Athena’s sideways landing left its drill unable to reach the Moon. At a roadside astronomy picnic, volunteers need help with a homemade lander display. Their drill has already completed the ground-contact phase.
Help haul the lander platform → You haul the platform until your shoulders ache. The picnic cheers its successful landing on the far side of the table.
Donate materials for the display → Your supplies secure the platform, earning the volunteers’ endorsement. Their procurement program now includes checking which way is up.
Record the actual mission result → You record the drill’s failure and the instruments that returned data. The volunteer retires a much simpler, less accurate disaster joke.
Scene: A volunteer indicates a homemade lander platform awaiting help, with a hand drill resting beside it. A modest drill bit already touches the picnic table beneath a tilted lunar-lander model.
Source: NASA Planetary Data System: CLPS TO PRIME-1 Athena (2025-03-06)
Source: NASA Intuitive Machines CLPS mission press kit
ENC-C04-B · Domestic adjectives
The FTC accused patriotic-goods sellers of false Made in USA claims and proposed a settlement. At a hardware shop, a worker is rebuilding a returned flag-display stand and invites help or materials. The advertising arrived entirely American. Several components apparently took a longer route.
Help haul the display sections → You haul the sections until your shoulders ache and enjoy the company. The flag needs a sturdy base more than another adjective.
Donate repair materials → Your materials secure the stand and earn trust. The worker records their actual source, an unexpectedly radical approach to product description.
Record the origin-claim distinction → You record the allegation and proposed settlement accurately. The worker removes an unsupported claim without needing to lower the flag.
Scene: A worker offers help with a stationary disassembled display stand beside unopened repair materials. A lavish blank patriotic product sleeve surrounds a pile of visibly mismatched ordinary components.
Source: FTC Announces Made in the USA Sweep (2026-04-14)
Source: Americana Liberty FTC case timeline: April 14, 2026
ENC-C04-C · Freedom from shade
At a travelling workers’ fair, Florida roofers show your crew the law blocking local heat protections. Their protest canopy covers the water cooler. A sponsor praising deregulation has put his chair underneath it. The roofers need help moving the display.
Help move the demonstration canopy → You haul the canopy until your arms ache. The roofers laugh as the sponsor follows its shadow without once supporting the policy.
Donate some water for workers → You donate some water; the roofers record your help. The sponsor calls hydration a personal responsibility, then asks whose cooler this is.
Record the roofers’ demonstration → You record the roofers explaining the Florida law. The sponsor keeps edging into the shot, specifically the shaded part.
Scene: Roofers point to a canopy awaiting repositioning while a sponsor sits beneath it and travelers watch. The anti-regulation sponsor's chair monopolizes the shade around the workers' cooler.
Editable overlays: “LOCAL HEAT RULES BLOCKED” — Blank display panel beside the canopy
Source: DeSantis signed Florida 2024 law barring local government heat/water-break mandates. This does not make drinking water illegal …
ENC-C05-A · Return to nonexistent sender
At a library stop, volunteers give your crew letters about the nonexistent studies in the first MAHA report. They offer some food for an accurate recorded reply. A retired postman has brought an empty envelope. “That’s all the research we could fit.”
Read and save the letters → You read and save the letters, laughing. The postman has underlined “address unknown” so hard the nonexistent study now has a window.
Record an accurate reply → You record the citation corrections and collect some food. The librarian checks the reply exists before pressing play.
Share some food; sort letters → You share some food and sort the letters with the volunteers. Every missing study gets a real paperclip. The science budget is recovering.
Scene: A retired postman holds an empty envelope open while a volunteer shows the travelers letters and available food. The prominently held envelope contains absolutely nothing; large stacks of actual correspondence surround it.
Editable overlays: “ADDRESS UNKNOWN” — Blank envelope front
Source: May 2025 reporting identified nonexistent studies and other citation problems in the initial MAHA report. HHS said citation and…
ENC-C05-B · Too big for the form
A community volunteer flags down your van with letters about the Pentagon accepting Qatar’s luxury jet. Her workplace made her declare a gifted muffin. She offers some food for a recorded reply. Her copy of the form asks whether the muffin has foreign owners.
Read and save the letters → You save the letters and laugh over the muffin declaration. The volunteer drew landing gear underneath it. Compliance rejected the extra wheels.
Record an accurate reply → You record the jet acceptance and collect some food. She declares the sandwiches herself. “No wings. We should be all right.”
Share some food; sort letters → You share some food and help sort letters. Someone folds the muffin form into an aircraft. Its gift exemption improves immediately.
Scene: A volunteer displays a blank gift form beside a plain muffin and gestures to letters for the crew. The modest muffin is surrounded by oversized paperwork and a small paper airplane.
Editable overlays: “GIFT DECLARATION” — Blank heading area on the muffin form
Source: The Pentagon announced on May 21, 2025 that it had accepted a Boeing 747 from Qatar for presidential use. Acceptance prompted l…
ENC-C05-C · The other dinner guests
After Trump’s dinner for top meme-coin investors, diner regulars have written their own requests for a hearing. They flag down your crew to carry them to D.C. The cook offers some food for a recorded reply. Their invitation is clipped to an unpaid gas bill.
Read and save their letters → You save the letters, laughing at the guest list. Occupation: dishwasher. Investment portfolio: a glove containing enough quarters for the laundry.
Record an accurate reply → You record their requests and collect some food. The cook announces the exclusive reception. It’s behind the counter, beside the mop.
Share some food; sort requests → You share some food and sort the requests. The regulars toast your arrival with tap water. Nobody checks its market capitalization.
Scene: Regulars show the travelers their invitation and blank letters while the cook indicates food available for the road. An elaborate homemade invitation is clipped to an ordinary unpaid bill beside a glove full of coins.
Editable overlays: “REQUEST FOR A HEARING” — Blank invitation panel
Source: Trump hosted top investors in his meme coin at his Virginia golf club on May 22, 2025; roughly 220 were invited. This establish…
ENC-C06-A · The coverage ladder
At a health-funding teach-in, volunteers show your stopped crew how the 2025 Medicaid law changes eligibility and spending. They’ve built a demonstration ladder. The bottom rung is labelled “taxpayer.” The first reachable rung has been removed to keep the model affordable.
Check the law and demonstration → You check the sources and understand the changes. The volunteer restores the missing rung for packing. Even the demonstration needs it to work.
Watch the volunteers rehearse → You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer playing a senator praises the ladder from a stepladder somebody else brought.
Scene: Volunteers point to the missing rung of an unoccupied display ladder while travelers observe. A separate sturdy stepladder stands behind the person praising the damaged model.
Editable overlays: “TAXPAYER” — Blank tag attached to bottom ladder support
Source: P.L.119-21 reduces projected federal Medicaid spending and changes eligibility. Projected insurance losses are projections, not…
ENC-C06-B · Priced by the department
Washington offered federal agencies Musk’s Grok AI for forty-two cents. At a roadside job fair, a host rehearses interviews with a talking toy and invites you to try. He asks whether human wages can also cover an entire department.
Check what the bargain actually buys → You explain the agency-access price, gaining trust and clarity. The host restores the wage column. The toy remains available at wholesale.
Try the practice interview → You quote your salary per entire department. The group laughs; the host admits that one person still expects one actual paycheck.
Scene: A host presents a talking toy beside a blank job board and invites the waiting travelers toward an empty interview chair. The tiny talking toy sits behind an enormous desk while the human interview chair is a folding stool.
Source: GSA and xAI Partner on $0.42 per Agency Agreement to Accelerate Federal AI Adoption (2025-09-25)
ENC-C06-C · The secondary title
Trump authorized “Department of War” as a secondary title. At a veterans’ hall stop, volunteers invite your crew to inspect their proposed response: rename the leaky roof “Air Superiority.” A bucket already controls the space beneath it.
Record the proposal and leak → You check the naming announcement and record the hall’s response. The veteran tips out the bucket. Air superiority has reached the carpet.
Join the naming rehearsal → You enjoy the rehearsal. The volunteer christens the mop “Strategic Deterrence.” The leak starts another drop while he’s still saluting.
Scene: Volunteers show a proposed blank roof-name card while a bucket catches an existing leak and travelers watch. A humble bucket occupies the exact territory claimed by an ambitious new title.
Editable overlays: “AIR SUPERIORITY” — Blank proposed name card beside the bucket
Source: September 2025 action authorized Department of War as a secondary title. Do not claim Congress abolished the statutory Departme…
ENC-C07-A · The peace division
FIFA gave Trump its first peace prize. A trophy repairer is adding a peace division between bowling and darts. He offers $10 and some food for lifting the display; repair materials and lunch company are welcome. The new department still needs shelf brackets.
Donate some repair materials → Your materials earn the repairer’s endorsement. The peace division acquires the modest structural support unavailable from an acceptance speech.
Lift the display for $10 and food → You earn cash, food, and sore muscles, laughing as world peace takes its place between a bowling ball and crossed darts.
Share food; record the award’s origin → You share lunch and record that FIFA created its own prize. The repairer keeps the Nobel label in a different drawer.
Scene: A repairer indicates a stationary trophy display and loose shelf brackets between bowling and dart trophies. A newly polished peace-themed cup has nowhere to stand between two crowded sports shelves.
Source: FIFA: President Donald J. Trump awarded inaugural FIFA Peace Prize (2025-12-05)
ENC-C07-B · Returned to the parents
Trump’s order to facilitate closing the Education Department has inspired a PTA’s “do it ourselves” fundraiser. They offer your stopped crew $10 and some food to shift donated desks. The volunteers have received local control. It came without a furniture dolly.
Donate supplies for the fundraiser → You donate some supplies; the PTA records your help. A parent attaches felt feet to a desk. Local control stops scratching the floor.
Take the desk-moving job → You earn $10 and some food with an aching back. A parent applauds. “Excellent. You’re now qualified to run the furniture department.”
Share some food; record concerns → You share some food and record the parents’ questions. They want to know which part of closing a department makes the desk lighter.
Scene: Parents assess desks awaiting relocation and show the travelers a blank job board. A large stack of desks sits beside a conspicuously absent dolly, represented only by an empty storage hook.
Editable overlays: “DESK MOVING: $10 + FOOD” — Blank job-offer board
Source: March 2025 EO directs the secretary to facilitate closure to extent permitted by law. Do not claim Congress actually abolished …
ENC-C07-C · Apparently overhead
At a research fundraiser opposing the Trump administration’s proposed NIH overhead cap, volunteers offer your crew $10 and some food to shift equipment. They also need supplies. The display labels the freezer “overhead.” A scientist is demonstrating what happens when overhead melts onto your shoes.
Donate supplies to the display → You donate some supplies; volunteers record your contribution. The scientist finally puts the thawing demonstration in a tray. Waste has stopped leaking.
Take the equipment-moving job → You earn $10 and some food, arms aching. Moving the empty freezer proves overhead weighs considerably more than the speech against it.
Share some food; record testimony → You share some food and record the scientist’s concerns. She points at the freezer plug. “The breakthrough is inside. It needs electricity.”
Scene: A scientist points to a tray beneath a safe demonstration freezer while volunteers offer the travelers a moving job. A freezer classified as overhead stands above a puddle from melting demonstration ice.
Editable overlays: “OVERHEAD • MOVING WORK $10 + FOOD” — Blank display board beside the empty freezer
Source: UT Southwestern estimated in February 2025 that the proposed cap risked over 100m yearly. Do not present the estimate or propos…
ENC-C08-A · Patriotic cartography
Trump’s Gulf renaming has left a roadside map club with old charts and new federal labels. They ask your stopped crew to help prepare a public comparison. The volunteer has carefully checked the coast. It has made no effort to move.
Donate supplies for comparison charts → You donate some supplies and help document the labels. The volunteer uses a ruler to confirm that greatness added no coastline.
Share some food with the club → You share some food, and everyone invents patriotic names for the crumbs. The plate becomes the first disputed territory to disappear.
Check and save the charts → You compare and save the charts, relieved to find the coordinates unchanged. The volunteer gives the compass permission to remain neutral.
Scene: A volunteer aligns two matching blank coast charts while travelers consider helping. Both charts share precisely the same shoreline beneath differently positioned blank title cards.
Editable overlays: “SAME COAST. NEW FEDERAL NAME.” — Editable header above the two blank charts
Source: January 2025 EO directed federal use of Gulf of America and restoration of Mount McKinley naming; it did not change geography o…
ENC-C08-B · A place at the table
